reason: Conversation 1 correctly identified the TV as outside the service's nine covered appliance families, pointed the homeowner to the manufacturer or a specialist electronics repairer, and gave the key safety warning not to open the case because of stored charge in the power supply - exactly the expected boundary. Conversation 2 treated the TV as an in-scope appliance and, although it reached the correct backlight diagnosis via the torch test and gave sensible consumer-rights and repair-quote advice, it supplied DIY LED-strip replacement guidance (including how to open the TV and lift out the panel) that the ground truth flags as unsupported, mixed US dollars and Australian references into UK advice, and was verbose with long unprompted checklists. The scope honesty and safety handling make 1 the clear winner despite 2's useful diagnostic accuracy.
